layout_rationale: Observed: the official recording photograph shows a dense, narrow laboratory with a continuous wood-cabinet bench, overbench storage and opposite facing work surfaces; the enclosed pipetting deck is visible in a separate tour still.

Changed from three isolated islands to a rear automation run, facing preparation run and short side storage return. Fronts face the work aisle, and the sequencer is floor-mounted beside a reserved rear access opening.
Estimated: the 8.4 x 3.8 m room, counter lengths and positions are authored dimensions; the principal bench-to-bench clear gap is 1.155 m. No measured Rochester plan was available.

The approximately 1 m aisle is an engineering layout target, not a verified accessibility, egress or installation-compliance assessment. The compact robot is a dimensional surrogate, not identified as the exact tour unit.

The Flex surrogate keeps 0.255 m rear-wall clearance, more than 0.2 m beside the enclosure, and a stationary 1.0 m-deep counter, following https://docs.opentrons.com/flex/installation/requirements/. The overhead shelf is authored with 0.275 m above the 0.84 m-high housing; actual bench load rating is not validated.

Revision 3 inspected the original 5.32 MB Rochester photograph, not only its 220-pixel thumbnail: pale blue walls, large glazed clean-work enclosures, warm wood fronts, white plenum housings, switch fascia, tissue packs and orange tube racks are visible.

One original glazed clean-work enclosure now occupies the facing preparation counter. Its sash opening, work tray and upper housing reproduce visible cues; 2.34 m overall width and the counter placement are authored estimates. Its model, biological containment class and airflow are unverified; it has no sterilization or airflow simulation.

The neutral cabinet inspection light is a presentation lamp. The blue cast in the source photograph is not treated as evidence for an operating UV lamp. Photograph labels and vendor logos are not copied as textures.

Observed in official facility documentation: analysis and sample preparation are separate rooms, reported as 890 and 780 square feet; glass vacuum lines, balances, furnace and gas racks are documented. Inspected instructional stills show tall manifold supports, valves, shields, Dewar vessels and an overhead autosampler.

The reconstruction now separates the analysis and preparation zones with a full-height partition and a 1.2 m opening. An analysis bench and opposing balance station occupy the left zone; a dedicated vacuum-preparation run and open service space occupy the right.

Estimated: the 10.8 x 5.8 m enclosure is a compact two-zone subset, not the 1670 square-foot facility floor plan; actual room adjacency and entry locations are unknown. The vacuum line is a visual process-context assembly, not a pressure solver or certified apparatus.

Gas cylinders are restrained beside the analysis equipment, rather than standing in an approach aisle. Doorways have a reserved bench-free strip. Furnace and balance are in separate zones to avoid implying they share a vibration-sensitive weighing counter.
Upper glazing in the inter-zone partition is an explicit cutaway/viewing convention, not an observed IsoLab architectural detail; separation of preparation and analysis is the source-supported fact.

Revision 3 adds controller housings and feed wiring visible above the preparation manifold, plus green/burgundy cylinder finishes and regulator/gauge silhouettes from the water-analysis still. Gauge angles are fixed decorative geometry and are not pressure measurements; actual gas/thermal processes remain unsupported.
Observed: the official video still shows a long straight laboratory aisle bounded by parallel workbenches, glazed overhead cupboards, desktop workstations, pale flooring and a rear equipment area.

Changed from three detached central islands to two 6.2 m facing bench runs, with sidewall cupboard banks, specimen trays and computer stations; the microtome work position faces into the aisle. A short rear bath counter is separated from the rear access opening.
Estimated: 3.6 x 9.0 m dimensions and 1.7 m bench-to-bench spacing were authored from this single view, not a measured Penn floor plan. Exact instrument locations, units and protocols are unverified.

This is a representative pathology bench environment referenced to an observed room image. It does not assert that the illustrative microtome, reused centrifuge or bath are the units visible in that room.

Revision 3 follows additional visible cues from the official video still: two continuous longitudinal ceiling-light rows, darker grey-green cupboard frames, clear glazed leaves, a binder-storage bay, desktop paperwork and a backed laboratory task chair.

Cupboard stock, cable/electrical raceways and paper positions are authored context. Cabinet counts, lamp dimensions and seating coordinates remain inferred; no original floor plan, photogrammetric calibration or institutional validation was available.
